title: Plugin Kit
summary: A typed plugin SDK and test harness for building versioned event-processing extensions.
intended_users: Open-source maintainers and application developers embedding third-party event processors.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Ad hoc plugins depended on host internals and could fail the entire event loop.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Dynamic scripting was rejected for type and sandbox ambiguity. Process isolation was documented as the next boundary for untrusted plugins but deferred for the hackathon scope.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Provide versioned Rust traits, explicit capabilities, and a reusable conformance harness.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: In-process plugins are fast and simple but are not a security sandbox.
design_decisions.repository_evidence: docs/architecture.md, docs/decisions.md, src/lib.rs, tests/conformance.rs, README.md, LICENSE, and CONTRIBUTING.md
design_decisions.validation_approach: Cargo tests specify compatibility negotiation, undeclared capability rejection, error containment, deterministic fixtures, and example-plugin conformance. Finch does not execute them.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Move untrusted plugins out of process when the threat model includes malicious native code.

testing_strategy: The conformance harness and integration fixtures cover public extension contracts, compatibility boundaries, capability refusal, and error containment.
security_threat: A buggy or malicious plugin requests undeclared capabilities or crashes the host path. Capability declarations, version checks, typed errors, panic containment guidance, and an explicit statement that in-process execution is not a sandbox. Residual risk: Native plugins still share process memory; hostile code requires process or WASM isolation.
production_limitation: The pilot supports one host language and does not provide hostile-code isolation.
technical_debt: Add a WASM adapter, compatibility matrix automation, and semver verification in release CI.
track_alignment_explanation: This is a reusable open-source SDK with a real extension surface, license, installation guidance, contribution path, and conformance tooling.
